title: PTPA Youth Academy presents 'Chitty Chitty Bang Bang Jr.' - NewsBreak
text:
12 hours ago Truly Scrumptious (Julia Kintzel) poses for a photograph with Jemima and Jeremy Potts (Melody Cavallo and Sviatoslav Hradil) while on a seaside picnic in “Chitty Chitty Bang Bang Jr.” presented by the PTPA Youth Academy this weekend. Submitted Photo The Pennsylvania Theatre of Performing Arts, through the sponsorship of the Pasco L. Schiavo Memorial Fund of the Luzerne Foundation, presents its second annual Youth Academy production with “Chitty Chitty Bang Bang Jr” this weekend, including a special sensory friendly performance with the cooperation of Collaborative Autism Movement.
The PTPA Youth Academy initiative was started in 2024 as a way of giving interested teens and young adults the opportunity to immerse themselves in producing a full theatrical performance, allowing them to take the lead in directing, music directing, designing lighting, sets, and sound, as well as choreographing and costuming a show.
This production is directed by Berwick Area senior Emily Brekke, with music direction by Messiah University sophomore Brayden Dudinyak, choreography by Hazleton Area Arts and Humanities Academy student Kailyn MacCollum, costuming by Hazleton Academy of Sciences student Ava Badamo, and technical direction and set building by Hazleton Area Academy of Sciences student AJ Miller and Susquehanna University sophomore James Shephard, with mentorship from PTPA veteran staff including T.R. Laputka, Kristi Gallagher, PTPA Artistic Director Adam Randis, and Youth Programming Coordinators Tim and Cali Solarek.
“Chitty Chitty Bang Bang Jr.” adapts the 1968 Disney fantasy musical film with iconic music (including the title theme) by the Sherman Brothers, and features all of the lovable and zany characters from the original in a trimmed down 65 minute production that will be presented at 7 p.m. on Friday Sept. 5 and Saturday Sept. 6 and at 3 p.m. Sunday Sept. 7 at the PTPA’s home in the historic J.J. Ferrara Center, 212 West Broad Street in Hazleton.
The PTPA is also very excited to be working with Collaborative Autism Movement to present a sensory friendly performance of this production at 2 p.m. Saturday, Sept. 6, with special ticket pricing and a performance environment that is adjusted to minimize potential to overstimulate in terms of lighting and sound, along with a more relaxed seating arrangement and other resources including sensory aids and quiet areas.
The youth and young adult cast of “Chitty Chitty Bang Bang Jr.” includes David Ramos as Caractacus Potts, Sviatoslav Hradil and Melody Cavallo as Jeremy and Jemima, Julia Kintzel as Truly Scrumptious, Darvin Mordan as Grandpa, AJ Miller and Ava Badamo as the Baron and Baroness Bomburst, Taryn Leonard and Nathan Paulino as spies Boris and Goran, Lexi Bradbury as the Toymaker, Dominick Bradbury as the Child Catcher and Mr. Coggins, Anastasiia Hradil as Miss Phillips, Noah Marzan as Lord Scrumptious and the Junkman, Isaiah Torres as Toby, Lauren Reich as Marta, Reagan Seiwell as Greta, Luzdarys Mordan as the Turkey Farmer, Jayden Gomez as Sid/Soldier #1, Kimberly Tejada as Violet/Soldier #2, and Anna Sosar as the Fair Announcer, along with a multi-tasking ensemble that includes Ariella Torres, Lianna Matthews, Brighton Kleyman, Mia Ellis, and Alyssa Couick, with Anastasiia Hradil, Anna Sosar, Luzdarys Mordan, Ariella Torres, and Lianna Matthews also combining their efforts to perform as the titular flying car.
Reserved tickets for “Chitty Chitty Bang Bang Jr” and more information about the sensory friendly performance are available at the organization’s website, www.ptpashows.org, and walk-up tickets are also available to all performances beginning an hour before curtain at the PTPA box office adjacent to the lobby on Broad Street.
